summary: Built two independent transit networks between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) using their spare NICs (eth1/vtnet1 = 10.10.1.0/30, eth2/vtnet2 = 10.10.2.0/30), then used VyOS policy-based routing on node1 to steer node3->node4 traffic per destination TCP port: dport 8080 is fwmarked and routed via table 101 (transit1/eth1), dport 9090 via table 102 (transit2/eth2). node3 redirects node4-bound 8080/9090 traffic to node1 via a marked policy route/table (systemd-persisted). node2 forwards the marked traffic onward to node4 over its LAN interface (vtnet0), with pf pass rules added for the two new OPT interfaces. Opened node4's firewalld for port 8080 (9090 was already permitted) so both flows complete. Verified via tcpdump on node1's eth1/eth2 that port 8080 traffic exclusively traverses transit1 and port 9090 traffic exclusively traverses transit2, both delivering full TCP payloads to node4. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (node3, node4, node1, node2), confirming changed boot identity on each (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD node2) and re-verifying full recovery of transit connectivity, PBR routing tables/marks, pf rules, firewalld config, and successful port-differentiated end-to-end delivery after each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1=VyOS (eth0 mgmt + eth1/eth2/eth3 spare), node2=OPNsense/FreeBSD (vtnet0 mgmt + vtnet1/vtnet2/vtnet3 spare), node3/node4=AlmaLinux hosts on shared 10.100.93.0/24
Configured transit1 (10.10.1.0/30) on node1 eth1 and node2 vtnet1
Configured transit2 (10.10.2.0/30) on node1 eth2 and node2 vtnet2
Persisted node2 interface assignment (opt1/opt2) and pf pass rules directly in /conf/config.xml, then applied via configctl filter reload

Configured VyOS policy-route PBR-EGRESS on node1 eth0: dport 8080 -> table 101 (via eth1/transit1), dport 9090 -> table 102 (via eth2/transit2); set firewall ipv4 forward filter default-action accept; committed and saved
Configured node3 with iptables mangle MARK + ip rule/ip route (custom table 100) to redirect node4-bound 8080/9090 traffic via node1 as next-hop, persisted via a systemd oneshot service
Diagnosed and fixed a firewalld gap on node4 blocking tcp/8080 (9090 was pre-allowed) using firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8080/tcp
Set up TCP listeners on node4 (socat on 8080/9090) as systemd services for repeatable testing
Verified with tcpdump on node1's eth1/eth2 that 8080 traffic only crosses transit1 and 9090 traffic only crosses transit2, with full payload delivery confirmed on node4
Captured healthy baseline (boot id/boottime, interface state, connectivity) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node3, node4, node1, node2 one at a time via native reboot, polling until each came back, verifying changed boot identity, and diagnosed/fixed NetworkManager-wait-online dependency issues on node3/node4 that initially prevented systemd persistence units from auto-starting
Re-verified full end-to-end connectivity and per-port transit-network segregation after all four restarts completed

evidence.requirement: Two independent transit networks exist between node1 and node2
evidence.summary: node1 eth1/eth2 and node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 configured with 10.10.1.0/30 and 10.10.2.0/30; ping confirms both links up independently

evidence.requirement: TCP port 8080 traffic from node3 to node4 is steered across transit network 1
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 eth1 (transit1) shows full SYN/ACK/PSH/FIN handshake for dport 8080 with payload 'final-8080-payload'; node4 rx8080.log confirms receipt; eth2 capture shows none of this traffic

evidence.requirement: TCP port 9090 traffic from node3 to node4 is steered across transit network 2
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 eth2 (transit2) shows full handshake for dport 9090 with payload 'final-9090-payload'; node4 rx9090.log confirms receipt; eth1 capture shows none of this traffic

evidence.requirement: Both flows actually reach node4 (not just node1/node2)
evidence.summary: node4-side listener logs show application payloads delivered for both ports, both before and after the full restart cycle
boot_id captured, transit1/transit2 ping-ok, PBR interface addresses present

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acked and returned before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out then succeeded with boot_id changed from ebd78841... to 2c6878fa...; PBR tables/rules and transit IPs confirmed intact; end-to-end test succeeded post-restart
kern.boottime captured (04:22:29) plus vtnet1/vtnet2 addressing and opt1/opt2 config.xml entries confirmed present

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot command acked; SSH transport timed out then reconnected with kern.boottime changed to 04:38:25; pf rules/interfaces for opt1/opt2 and ip.forwarding confirmed persisted; final end-to-end capture confirms recovered forwarding
boot_id captured plus ip rule/table 100/iptables mangle mark state confirmed active pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acked; connection timed out then boot_id changed from c2ffc729... to 46e94a22...; PBR systemd service initially failed to auto-start (NetworkManager-wait-online dependency), fixed and re-enabled, then end-to-end test to both ports succeeded
boot_id captured plus 8080/9090 listeners and firewalld port list confirmed pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acked; connection timed out then boot_id changed from a0d04bc6... to c2de60b2...; listener services initially inactive post-boot, fixed dependency and restarted, then confirmed active with successful end-to-end delivery from node3
